findings.summary: Cheliped field report (twice-reproduced live 2026-08-16): the guard auto-imported a lock stamped with the fallback owner 'claude-hook', but the unlock CLI's ownership check computes 'local-worktree-<hash>' and can never match it, so clear_lock REFUSED for every session and the only escape was `rm .git/tdd-playbook/active-lock.json` — a hard cross-session deadlock in the strongest anti-gaming guard, F2-blocked from any in-session fix.
findings.disposition: Root fix (the architecture-adversary's deeper seam, not my first synthesized-string draft): cmd_unlock now passes expected_session_id=<real env token, or None>; an env-less unlock SKIPS the session check and ownership falls to the worktree_id check clear_lock ALREADY performs — so a fallback-owned lock (INCLUDING an already-wedged 'claude-hook' one whose source_worktree_id still matches) is releasable by a plain same-worktree unlock, forward AND backward. The three divergent session-id fallbacks (test_lock_guard/tdd_lock/red_lock) are unified through host_contract.session_id so no new claude-hook locks are minted. Two red-first tests in the blessed suite replay the exact wedged-lock shape (guard-imported legacy lock + on-disk claude-hook lock); both release cleanly, in-root locked-test edits still BLOCK.

findings.summary: The report asked for a legal recovery path to replace `rm`. As first planned, `unlock --force` would have shipped with the `forced` flag as a write-only field (neither /grade nor gate_yield read it — integration Finding 1), undiscoverable (the refusal/hints/tdd-unlock.md never point to it — Finding 2), and unable to clear a corrupt/schema-mismatched lock (arch Finding 3), so `rm` would have survived for that family.
findings.disposition: unlock --force skips the ownership check but KEEPS the generation/lock_id CAS; force_unlink_lock raw-clears a lock _validate_lock cannot even read (the corrupt/schema family, so `rm` is retired for it too). It composes with the reason(>=10)/class gates (recovery is audited, not a bypass) and journals forced:true — now READ by /grade (grade.md). The 'owned by another session' refusal, and tdd-unlock.md, point to --force explicitly (not `rm`). Security-adversary CONFIRMED --force is the MOST visible unlock (strictly worse for a cheater than a plain unlock) and opens no test-editing escape; added session_downgrade:true journaling for the one release the fix newly permits (env-less same-worktree clear of a real-token lock). Tested: cross-session, corrupt-lock, reason-gate composition, journal consumer, and the hardening flag.

findings.summary: Cheliped Defect C residual: under a version skew (an older vendored guard reading a lock a newer CLI wrote), active_lock sets _contract_error and main() failed closed on EVERY write — including OUT-OF-ROOT memory/plan/scratchpad writes, re-opening the same cross-session DoS the v1.37.0 edit_findings fix closed, but on an earlier branch; and the block message was opaque ('canonical authority repaired').
findings.disposition: main()'s _contract_error branch now bows out (emit clean-allow) for out-of-root non-Bash targets even in the repair state, and names the actionable remedy ('hook/CLI version mismatch — update tdd-playbook and reload') on a schema_version mismatch. Red-first against both directions (out-of-root PASSES; in-root names the remedy). NOT the report's 'degrade to warn on in-root writes' — that weakens the guard during the skew window; the real remedy is version alignment, which the message points at.

findings.summary: The field report's Defect B ('stale lock never self-invalidates') proposed auto-expiring a lock when imported_from is missing or HEAD has moved, plus a TTL on lock-transaction.lock. Verified against the code, all three are NORMAL healthy states, and auto-expiring on them would be a regression.
findings.disposition: Rejected WITH evidence (both plan adversaries independently affirmed): import RENAMES .claude/tdd-lock.json to .migrated so imported_from-missing is the normal post-import state (and native locks never set imported_from at all); a TEST-LOCK spans commits by design, so HEAD-moved is normal and expiring on it would let an agent bypass the guard by committing (gate-by-proxy on a fact the agent controls); lock-transaction.lock is a persistent flock target the OS auto-releases on process exit, so a stale file holds nothing. The one genuine deferral — a downstream version-echo so a wedged repo can tell fixed-from-wedging-1.30.0 (integration Finding 5) — is recorded as dated integration_debt (test-lock-deadlock-fix-version-echo, owner david, exp 2026-11-15), not silently dropped.
